body:
1. Java Threads

A thread is a lightweight subprocess, the smallest unit of processing, allowing concurrent execution of program parts.

2. Java Virtual Machine (JVM)

The JVM acts as a run-time engine that loads, verifies, and executes bytecode while providing a runtime environment.

3. Pillars of OOPs

The four pillars are Inheritance, Polymorphism, Encapsulation, and Abstraction, which form the basis of object-oriented programming.

4. String vs StringBuilder

String is immutable (cannot be changed), whereas StringBuilder is mutable and efficient for frequent modifications.

5. Interface vs Abstract Class

Interfaces support multiple inheritance and abstract methods, while abstract classes can have constructors and concrete methods.

6. Exception Handling

A mechanism to handle runtime errors using try, catch, finally, throw, and throws to maintain application flow.

7. JDK vs JRE vs JVM

JDK is the dev kit (tools + JRE), JRE provides libraries to run apps, and JVM is the engine that executes bytecode.
code:
// JDK = JRE + Development Tools
// JRE = JVM + Library Classes

8. Static Keyword

The static keyword means a member belongs to the class itself rather than an instance of the class.

9. Constructors

A constructor is a special method used to initialize objects; it has no return type and shares the class name.

10. Final Keyword

The final keyword restricts users: variables become constants, methods cannot be overridden, and classes cannot be inherited.

11. Array vs ArrayList

Arrays are fixed in size, whereas ArrayList is a dynamic collection that grows or shrinks automatically.

12. Overloading vs Overriding

Overloading happens within the same class (different parameters), while Overriding occurs in a subclass (same signature).
